regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India's GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters on first read — but IIP fell to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, core sector slipped to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%, and manufacturing PMI eased to 52.8 from 53.5. The services PMI at 54.5 is doing the heavy lifting; goods-economy proxies are losing altitude. The inversion: if capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is genuinely rising, why is IIP decelerating? The answer is base effects and a mix shift toward services — not broad-based industrial acceleration.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY masks a dangerous internal split: core CPI at 3.9% YoY is contained, but fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print — is feeding directly into WPI at 9.92% YoY. The gap between core and headline is not comfort; it is a pipeline. WPI-to-CPI transmission typically runs with a two-quarter lag, meaning today's fuel shock becomes Q2 FY27's core problem. The RBI's own inflation forecast has already moved to 5.1% YoY — 60bps above its comfort ceiling.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits — 75th percentile historically — makes structural, not cyclical. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals non-bank lenders filling the gap, but wholesale funding dependency is rising precisely as US 10Y yields sit at 5.26%. The last time India's CD ratio sustained above 80% during a global rate spike, macro-prudential tightening followed within three quarters.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is on hold, but the real rate calculus is deteriorating: with headline CPI at 4.45% YoY and the RBI's own forecast at 5.1% YoY, the ex-ante real rate is barely positive and shrinking. A rate cut here would be a gift to inflation; a hike would stress the CD ratio further. The RBI is pinned — and INR at 96.15 with US 10Y at 5.26% means the FX defence is doing the tightening work the repo rate cannot.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity from 75.6% is the most credible signal of a genuine investment cycle — not budgeted capex, but actual machine orders. The contradiction: core sector growth at 5.4% YoY is decelerating, and manufacturing PMI at 52.8 is softening. Private capex typically accelerates above 80% capacity utilisation; at 77.4%, the incentive exists but the trigger has not yet fired. Watch cement and steel dispatch for confirmation.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong print, but the prior month was ₹1,74,116 cr — a 14.8% sequential jump that warrants scrutiny for advance filing effects rather than pure demand. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY confirm that urban and semi-urban demand is real. The divergence to watch: credit card growth has collapsed to 2.3% YoY from 5.6%, suggesting the mass-market consumer is tapping out even as the affluent segment drives vehicle and discretionary spend.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 630 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months: deposits lagging credit acceleration signals funding stress. NBFC credit growth at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY) shows non-bank lenders compensating, but wholesale funding dependency rising.","implication":"Overweight private sector banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity tightening will force margin compression. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure, not growth concerns. Position for a 50 bps cut by June.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile is historically mid-cycle stress. In 2022–23, similar ratios preceded RBI's rate-cut cycle. Deposit growth at 44th percentile is weak relative to credit appetite.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Breaks 77% — Capex Cycle Firm","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals strong investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) — 74th percentile historically — indicates headroom for capex without inflationary pressure. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior month) is moderating but remains positive. Manufacturing PMI at 52.8 index (down from 53.5) shows order books intact despite slight momentum loss.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Capex cycle is self-reinforcing: 77% utilisation triggers new capacity orders. Expect IIP capital goods to sustain 12–16% growth through Q3 FY27. Avoid cyclical stocks trading at >18x forward PE; capex upcycles compress multiples as supply normalises.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77% is mid-cycle, historically preceding 18–24 months of sustained capex. Last similar reading in 2021 preceded the 2022–23 capex boom.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP AUM Hits ₹18.62 lakh cr — Affluent Inflection","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (up from ₹31,961 cr / month), rising 2 consecutive months. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (up from ₹18.21 lakh cr) — 93rd percentile historically. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn) at 82nd percentile. MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (up from ₹85.76 lakh cr), rising 2 in a row at 86th percentile. Equity MF net inflows at ₹29,329 cr / month (up from ₹24,697 cr / month).","implication":"SIP AUM growing 40% faster than SIP account growth (2.3% vs 1.1% monthly) signals affluent money entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour — average ticket size rising. Rotate from small-cap to large-cap, quality dividend payers. Expect SIP growth to decelerate to 8–10% by Q4 FY27 as base effects normalise.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile is near all-time highs. In 2021, similar AUM levels preceded a 12-month consolidation. Retail equity participation is at peak saturation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile — Import Bill Risk","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY) — 95th percentile historically. Brent crude at $98.35 / bbl (flat from $98.35 / bbl) but trending higher: recent sequence shows $97.41 → $97.47 → $97.44 → $98.93 → $99.05 → $96.10. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% YoY) driven by fuel. India's oil import bill at elevated levels; CAD pressure building if Brent sustains above $100 / bbl.","implication":"Hedge INR weakness — fuel inflation will keep RBI's rate-cut cycle constrained. Monitor CAD trajectory; current account deficit risk if oil stays elevated.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is extreme. In 2022, similar levels preceded RBI's aggressive tightening cycle. Current 22.93% is unsustainable without policy response.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US 10Y Yield at 5.26% — Carry Trade Unwind Risk","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.26% yield (up from 5.24% yield) — 95th percentile historically. Recent sequence: $4.94 → $5.01 → $4.96 → $5.18 → $5.17 → $5.24, rising 3 of last 5 observations. Fed funds rate at 3.63% p.a. (flat, 67th percentile). BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a.) — 86th percentile, signalling tightening. In 2023, similar yields preceded a 15% EM equity drawdown. Current level is unsustainable for carry trades.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Masks GCC Consolidation","data_text":"Office absorption at 5.2 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 4.1 mn sq ft / quarter) but scored at -100 (strong-negative signal). Recent sequence: 26.9 → 13.2 → 4.9 → 11.6 → 13.7 → 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter shows violent volatility, not growth. Office vacancy at 16% vacant (up from 14.5%) — 50th percentile. Yet Bengaluru office rent at ₹163 / sqft / mo (up from ₹148 / sqft / mo) — 95th percentile, rising 3 of last 5 observations. Nifty IT index flat while office rents surge 10% YoY.","implication":"Traditional IT services are NOT the office buyer anymore. Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and non-IT corporates are consolidating premium space in Bengaluru, Mumbai. This decouples commercial RE from IT stock performance. Overweight commercial REIT exposure (Embassy, Mindspace) on GCC demand, not IT services. Underweight Nifty IT — rent inflation benefits REITs, not IT companies. If Nifty IT remains flat while office rents hit 95th percentile, the disconnect is structural, not cyclical.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Office rent at 95th percentile with flat IT stocks is a 2-year divergence. In 2022–23, IT stocks and office rents moved together. Current decoupling signals GCC-driven demand replacing IT services as the marginal buyer.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry GDP While Goods Economy Loses Altitude

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY — but IIP fell to 6.7% YoY from 8.8% YoY and core sector slipped to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% YoY; goods-economy proxies are decelerating.
  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is services-led: PMI Services rose to 54.5 while PMI Manufacturing eased to 52.8 from 53.5.
  • GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month — up from ₹1,74,116 cr / month — is a 14.8% sequential jump; advance filing effects likely explain a portion of the beat.
  • But two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY confirm genuine mass-market demand, even as credit card growth collapses to 2.3% YoY from 5.6% YoY.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY and GST at a record print suggest broad expansion; IIP deceleration and credit card collapse suggest the goods economy and mass-market credit are already softening beneath the headline.

Bottom line: Watch IIP capital goods for a second consecutive deceleration — if it prints below 12% YoY next month, the capex narrative loses its primary evidence.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Euro Stoxx at All-Time Highs — Growth Data Says Otherwise

The facts:

  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,269 (100th percentile) — pricing perfection — while Eurozone GDP is only 1.2% YoY and Eurozone CPI re-accelerated to 3.3% YoY from 2.9% YoY.
  • US PMI Composite at 56.0 (84th percentile) diverges from US GDP SAAR slowing to 2.2% SAAR from 2.5% SAAR; surveys and output are telling different stories.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.26% yield (95th percentile) with Fed Funds at 3.63% p.a. — a 163bps inversion — means bond markets are tightening conditions the Fed has not formally endorsed.
  • But China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) with GDP at 4.3% YoY from 5.0% YoY removes the commodity-reflation backstop that DM equity bulls are implicitly assuming.

The tension: DM equity indices are at or near all-time highs; underlying nominal growth is decelerating in both the US and China, and real tightening is already embedded in the 10Y yield. The surveys are the trapdoor.

Bottom line: Hedge DM equity exposure: if US 10Y breaches 5.35% yield, the equity risk premium compression that drove the S&P 500 to 7,652 reverses mechanically.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record — But Funded by Shrinking Deposit Base

The facts:

  • DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr / month (100th percentile, rising 2 in a row) and SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile) are providing a structural bid to Indian equities.
  • MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile) with SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile) — the affluent household is systematically rotating from deposits to mutual funds.
  • But deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against bank credit at 17.1% YoY means the same household rotation that funds SIP inflows is draining the deposit base banks need to lend.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr / month (83rd percentile) has reversed — but US 10Y at 5.26% yield makes this reversal fragile; carry economics deteriorate above 5.25% yield.

The tension: Record domestic flows into equities and the deposit-to-MF rotation are two sides of the same coin: the liquidity that looks strong in equity markets is the liquidity that is missing from bank balance sheets.

Bottom line: Monitor FII flows weekly — a reversal back to net selling above ₹15,000 cr / month outflow would expose the market to a DII absorption test at current SIP run-rates.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Premium Demand Holds — REITs Price Office Stress

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING: NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 15%, +5 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) sustain purchasing power.
  • Launch mix skewed premium-to-luxury: premium (₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr) at 34% of supply and luxury (₹1.5–2.5 cr) at 24% — affordable (14% of launches.
  • Bengaluru leads residential with sales 12% YoY and price growth 8% YoY; NCR prices up 12% YoY despite sales at -1% YoY — supply discipline, not demand, is holding prices.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior prints — office REIT market pricing the vacancy risk that Bengaluru rents at ₹163/sqft/mo have not yet confirmed.

The tension: Physical office rents in Bengaluru at a 95th-percentile ₹163/sqft/mo signal pricing power; REIT unit prices down 15–22% from prior levels signal the listed market sees vacancy risk and rising US yields as the dominant frame.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until office vacancy stabilises below 14% vacant nationally — at 16% vacant and rising, the yield compression thesis requires a rate cut that is not coming.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — US Yields Hold the Match

The facts:

  • US 10Y at 5.26% yield (95th percentile, rising 3 of last 5 observations) — if sustained above 5.25% yield, EM carry unwinds accelerate and FII equity flows reverse from the current ₹29,631 cr / month net inflow.
  • Brent at $98.35/bbl trending toward $100/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill, widens CAD by ~40 bps, and feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag; fuel inflation already at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile).
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with credit growing at 17.1% YoY vs deposits at 10.8% YoY — NBFC wholesale funding stress is the second-order risk if global rates stay elevated.
  • But INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) with RBI defending the 96 level — FX reserve adequacy is the buffer; a break above 97 would signal reserve depletion is accelerating.

The tension: All three domestic risks — oil, credit stress, and INR — have a single external trigger: US 10Y yields. A move above 5.35% yield tightens all three simultaneously, and India has no policy rate room to respond.

Bottom line: Watch US 10Y yield this week — a close above 5.35% yield is the threshold that forces RBI FX intervention, pressures NBFC funding costs, and tests DII absorption capacity in a single session.

"}
